text:
Ellie: Quick design check 1 0 — playground streaming behaviour + compact controls prototype.
Ellie: Problem: when a stream pauses (network or model backpressure) the UI keeps appending tiny fragments. Users think it's frozen. Proposal: collapse trailing fragments into a single inline "stream paused" chip with a lightweight verbatim count and a resume/regenerate affordance.
Mark: Nice. For voiceover, we can't keep reading tiny deltas. I suggest using aria-live=polite for fragments and then when we collapse emit a single announcement: "Stream paused, 34 tokens buffered. Controls available."
Priya: Agree with Mark. Also: mobile UX — long-press on a message should reveal the same set of actions (Resume | Stop | Copy | Pin tokens). That avoids floating controls eating screen real estate.
Owen: Long-press is good. On desktop we have three options for control placement:
- inline micro-actions under bubble (compact)
- floating vertical toolbar to the right (minimal clutter)
- overflow menu on message kebab (discoverable but hidden)
Which do we prefer?
Ellie: I prefer floating toolbar for long responses and inline actions for short ones. Could be responsive: threshold by char/count.
Priya: Microcopy thoughts for the chip: "Stream paused  34 tokens buffered", "Partial output (34 tokens)" or "Output delayed  34 tokens queued". I lean toward "Stream paused" because "partial" feels ambiguous.
Mark: +1 for "Stream paused". Also add an accessible label: aria-label="Stream paused, 34 tokens buffered. Actions: resume, stop, copy."
a11y-bot: Accessibility nits: ensure the chip is focusable (tabindex=0), keyboard-friendly controls, and tooltips appear on focus as well as hover. Use role="status" for the collapsed announcement and ensure announcements are rate-limited.
Owen: Implementation details: the stream meta includes buffered_tokens and estimated_remaining_tokens. We could show a tiny progress hint (e.g. 34/120 tokens, or a percent) but keep it subtle: small gray text "34 tks (28% done)". Do we want percent?
Priya: Percentage can mislead (models don't always have strict lengths). Maybe show "~28%" with a tilde and only when we have reasonable confidence (>60% estimate confidence).
Ellie: Good caveat. Telemetry: events to add: playground.stream_pause, playground.resume_clicked, playground.stop_clicked, playground.longpress_actions. Payload: { buffered_tokens, est_remaining, trigger } (trigger: network|user|runtime).
Mark: Keyboard shortcuts: resume = Ctrl/Cmd+Enter, stop = Esc, open actions = Shift+K. Add shortcut hints next to buttons when screen width allows.
Owen: Styling: chip should use high-contrast border for dark mode and 2px focus ring. On small screens chip becomes full-bleed row with actions stacked.
a11y-bot: Also: check NVDA/VoiceOver behavior for frequent updates; prefer announcing only on state change. Provide a snippet for devs:
```
// announce once on pause
const pauseRegion = document.getElementById('pause-announcer');
pauseRegion.textContent = `Stream paused, ${buffered} tokens buffered.`;
// ensure aria-live polite on small updates
chunkRegion.setAttribute('aria-live', 'polite');
```
Priya: For token visibility: show a faint "22 tks" tag near the timestamp; allow a pin toggle (pin keeps it visible per-user). Tooltip text: "Token usage for this response" and must be focusable.
Ellie: Copy for regen button options: "Regenerate", "Resume", "Retry". I think "Regenerate" implies a fresh output; "Resume" implies continuing from buffer. We should surface both: if candidate resumes are supported show "Resume"; otherwise show "Regenerate".
Mark: UX experiment idea: A/B test resume vs regenerate wording and toolbar vs inline micro-actions. Instrument retention and confusion metrics.
Owen: I'll mock a responsive toolbar + long-press sheet in Figma and push a preview. Preview link: https://figma.com/file/PLAYGROUND/streaming-controls (internal).
Ellie: Timeline: Owen to push prototype by EOD, Mark to add keyboard spec, Priya to finalize a11y announce wording, I'll write the tiny product brief for PM signoff.
deploy-bot: demo branch created: playground/compact-stream-chip  preview: https://preview.redwood.ai/playground/compact-stream-chip
Ellie: Thanks! Ping here when preview is ready for review. :eyes:
